dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Who, cái gì, where, when, tại sao - these words are so difficult to learn in tiếng Việt. Why do Vietnamese people have to dùng so many complex question words?

dialogue.speaker: Michael
dialogue.text: Actually, the question words in tiếng Việt are very logical. "Who" for people, "cái gì" for objects, and "tại sao" helps understand reasons. What part do you find difficult?

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: I understand cái gì is "what," but sometimes Vietnamese people also dùng "gì" alone. And when do we dùng "tại sao" versus when to dùng "vì sao"? Too many ways to ask the same thing!

dialogue.speaker: Michael
dialogue.text: That's true, but that richness makes tiếng Việt interesting. It's like chess, different moves but the same purpose. Would you like me to teach you how to dùng these words?

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: You're comparing language to chess? That's surprising... But I like it. Tại sao do you know so much about tiếng Việt? You can teach me, but don't act like a teacher.

dialogue.speaker: Michael
dialogue.text: Because I'm Vietnamese-American, so tiếng Việt is part of who I am. I can help you understand "cái gì" and "tại sao" through real situations. Where would you like to học? There's a quiet café nearby...
